{"m": "gpt-4o", "msg": [{"content": "You compare short personal anecdotes by their underlying relational structure - the pattern of intentions, causes, deceptions, reversals, and outcomes among the people involved - NOT by their surface topic, setting, or vocabulary. Two stories can be about totally different situations yet share the same deep structure; two stories can share the same topic yet have opposite structure.", "role": "system"}, {"content": "SITUATION:
I told my coworker Sarah about my salary negotiation strategy in confidence. The next day, she went to our manager and used my exact arguments to negotiate her own raise first, making it impossible for me to use the same approach. She smiled at me in the hallway like nothing happened.

CANDIDATE A:
My college roommate asked to read my grad school application essay for 'feedback.' A week later, I discovered he'd submitted an essay to the same program using my personal story about my grandfather—the unique hook I'd spent months crafting. He got in. I didn't.

CANDIDATE B:
I shared my salary negotiation strategy with my coworker Sarah, hoping she'd also advocate for herself. She used similar arguments in her own negotiation and got a raise. When I tried the same approach later, it worked for me too. She actually thanked me for the advice.

Which candidate shares the same underlying relational structure as the SITUATION (ignore surface topic similarity)? Respond as JSON: {"choice": "A" or "B", "reason": "<one sentence>"}.", "role": "user"}], "t": 0.0, "tag": "exp2:2"}
content: {"choice": "A", "reason": "Both involve betrayal where a confidant uses shared information for personal gain, undermining the original sharer's opportunity."}
